limitations: Ten adult macaques of both sexes include Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis, aged 5.5-16.5 years. Neuronal double labeling was examined 32 days after the last of five injections in PFA-fixed 40-micrometre cryosections. Fluorophore reversal, omitted-primary controls and Figure 2c-d address staining and channel artifacts. They do not establish lineage, complete specificity or quantified sensitivity. Antibody omission is not a biological no-neurogenesis control, and no matched dose-control experiment establishes BrdU safety.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

studies.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

studies.correctionCheck: PMC scientific text, PubMed/Europe PMC metadata and exact DOI/title correction, erratum and retraction searches were checked on 14 September 2026. No notice resolving the protocol or allocation questions was identified; this is not exhaustive surveillance.
studies.finding: The reported marker combinations support adult macaque dentate neuronal and oligodendroglial production under the labeling assumptions. They do not identify a universal rate, common multipotent founder, observed migration, replacement feedback or cognitive function.
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
limitations: Ten adult macaques of both sexes include Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis, aged 5.5-16.5 years. The paper does not provide an animal-by-species, sex, age, dosing, survival and assay manifest. Ten injected animals do not establish ten independent animals for every neuronal or glial endpoint.

Intravenous BrdU was 50 mg/kg, either once or daily for five consecutive days, administered between 09:00 and noon. Materials and Methods lists survival times ending at 72 days, whereas Results twice gives 75 days as the maximum. The reference injection for that discrepancy is not reconciled; neither value is silently selected.

BrdU and PCNA label DNA synthesis or cell-cycle-associated profiles; they do not continuously observe completed cytokinesis or a clone. PCNA was examined in sections from the same brains, not as a second independent animal cohort or a reported same-cell BrdU/PCNA lineage assay. Apposed doublets suggest, but do not identify, sibling relationships.

Early and later regional labeling is compared across sacrificed animals. BrdU-positive cells at the longest interval are not specifically identified as neurons. Label retention does not establish the survival fraction of a birth cohort, a neuron-specific lifespan, absence of rapid turnover elsewhere or absence of BrdU toxicity.

Neuronal double labeling was examined 32 days after the last of five injections in PFA-fixed 40-micrometre cryosections. Twenty nonadjacent sections were examined for each of NeuN and TuJ1; these are section counts, not independent animals. Exact biological replication, section sampling, denominators and uncertainty are not supplied for the reported averages.

BrdU/NeuN and BrdU/TuJ1 are alternative marker assays, not a reported three-marker identity for every labeled cell. The study reports neuronal colabels in GCL/SGZ and none in the other examined hippocampal regions; sampling and marker sensitivity do not establish absolute regional absence. Raw confocal stacks, optical section positions and segmentation have not been reanalysed.

Fluorophore reversal, omitted-primary controls and Figure 2c-d address staining and channel artifacts. They do not establish lineage, complete specificity or quantified sensitivity. Antibody omission is not a biological no-neurogenesis control, and no matched dose-control experiment establishes BrdU safety.

O4 or CNP double labeling used sequential black nuclear and brown cytoplasmic peroxidase signals in ethanol-fixed paraffin sections of 8 or 10 micrometres. Figure 3 shows 27-day single-injection examples. These preparations are distinct from the 32-day neuronal fluorescence assay; marker-positive morphology does not measure myelin formation or conduction.

Astrocyte generation is attributed to Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) and Eriksson et al. (1998), not a newly reported GFAP assay in this experiment. Finding several phenotypes near one niche does not establish a shared multipotent founder, self-renewal or exclusive stem-cell lineage. The 1988 GFAP/autoradiographic assays are separately reviewed and do not trace a common founder.

The approximately 1,000 BrdU/TuJ1-positive cells per hippocampus is extrapolated from about two profiles per section, 40-micrometre sections and an approximately 19-mm external anatomical length. Scaling by an external 4.8-million-neuron estimate and dividing by five injections gives the provisional 0.004% per day. This is not a direct daily birth count or an unbiased whole-hippocampus stereological census.

Five-day cumulative labeling followed by 32 days of survival combines labeling opportunity, subsequent division, dilution, survival and marker expression. A single retained-label estimate does not identify production and death separately. The paper itself leaves lower production versus lower survival unresolved. No empirical edge weight or universal rate is assigned.

The roughly tenfold rodent comparison uses a separate published mouse study and external denominators. The paper acknowledges unmatched age, species, environment, labeling and survival procedures. Absolute-age and relative-age hypotheses were not compared in one matched design, and this series supplies no invariant primate-to-human scaling.

Bipolar morphology and radial or tangential orientation support a migration interpretation but do not track displacement, origin or a radial-glial guidance interaction. Nearby cells are not a clone, and anatomical resemblance to developing neurons is not an executed construction rule.

The replacement interpretation draws on separate human neuron counts and macaque synapse counts. Synapse-count stability is not a matched neuron census. This experiment measures neither paired births and deaths, feedback of population state, replacement identity nor the fraction of older neurons ultimately renewed.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

studies.finding: Adult CpG site-16 patterns followed foster-care class. TSA altered several molecular readouts and the low-care group stress response, with site-specific and group-specific differences.
limitations: Long-Evans rat hippocampus is bulk tissue containing neurons and glia. High/low licking-grooming and arched-back nursing groups are selected extremes of continuous maternal behavior, not universal biological classes.

Cross-fostering changes a postnatal care environment. It does not isolate licking from nursing, nutrition or other maternal effects, directly manipulate an abstract neural state, or establish germline inheritance. Same-class foster controls are other mothers, not untouched biological-mother controls.

General adult-age statements conflict with assay-specific 90-day descriptions. ChIP figures report four animals/group but supplementary fixed-tissue methods specify six. GR protein Figure 5a reports five but Western methods specify six. Clones and technical blot replicates are not independent animals; litter dependence remains relevant.

Exon 1_7 is an alternative first exon of the rat glucocorticoid receptor gene. CpG site 16 at the 5-prime end of the NGFI-A binding region and site 17 at its 3-prime end have different outcomes. Bisulfite cytosine readouts, acetyl-H3K9-associated ChIP, NGFI-A ChIP, GR protein and plasma corticosterone are separate observables.

TSA infusion is a broad pharmacological intervention, not a locus-specific methylation edit or cell-specific neural manipulation. The restraint-stress cohort is separate from the GR-protein cohort. Parallel effects do not identify their causal mediation order.

The published Figure 2-associated t/P pairs (2.1/P<0.001 and 3.1/P<0.0001) are inconsistent with ordinary t tests; exact uncertainty is not reproduced. The 27 July 2004 publisher correction fixes labels, corticosterone units to micrograms/dL and bisulfite PCR annealing to 56 degrees C; the supplement retains conflicting text.

Individual animal source values and clone sequences are unavailable in the reviewed materials. Published findings are not an independent reproduction, and nonsignificant contrasts are not equivalence tests.

limitations: Bilateral hippocampal antisense injections reduce the named transporter in tissue. They are not genetically restricted to a cell class. Astrocytic MCT4 and neuronal MCT2 attribution uses expression evidence; direct cell-to-cell lactate flux was not measured in these behavioral assays.

ODNs were injected 1 h before training; rescue L-lactate (100 nmol) or equicaloric glucose (50 nmol) was injected 15 min before training. Retention was tested at 24 h and 7 days, with 1 h short-term testing in a separate MCT2 assay.

The behavioral endpoint is inhibitory-avoidance entry latency. Supplementary animal, surgical and task procedures and Tables S4-S5 remain unread: age, sex, shock protocol and exact group statistics are not independently established here.

Figure 6 and the MCT2 Results report no lactate rescue; a Discussion sentence inconsistently lists MCT2 among rescued knockdowns. Other Results sentences pair significant impairment with p > 0.05. No numerical inference is derived from those inconsistent passages.

Rescue does not uniquely establish lactate as an exclusive energy substrate; redox, signaling and other metabolic explanations remain possible. The failed equicaloric glucose rescue is dose- and protocol-specific, not proof that glucose can never support retention.

limitations: Both sexes were used. Long-term eyelid closure starts around P15 and ends at P32. Deprivation changes sensory experience during development; it is not a selective manipulation of myelin, nor elimination of all retinal activity.

CC1 cell counts, NG2-CreERT2/tau-mGFP internodes after P19 tamoxifen, and isolated optic-nerve compound action potentials use distinct assay preparations. They cannot be collapsed into measurements of one axon or a directly identified mediator.
Conduction velocity is nerve length divided by stimulus-to-CAP-peak latency at room temperature. CAP width describes a population waveform, not an identified single-axon speed or information code.

The main text and Figure 3 caption differ on the deprived internode median; Figure 7 repeats Figure 3 group labels, medians and sample counts despite a separate genetic assay. Figure 2 text/caption swap myelinated-axon percentages, and the reported conduction percentage does not directly match the caption means. Exact quantitative calibration remains unadmitted.

Internodes and axons are nested within mice. Raw measurements, animal-clustered uncertainty and plotted values have not been independently reproduced. Ultrastructural and paired-pulse nulls do not prove full equivalence.

studies.finding: Behavior varies with assigned complexity and additional stimulus features; location and grouping readouts coexist with constituent and matched-pair nulls.
limitations: The same 20 adults performed all parts in fixed order after passing sequence training in under 20 minutes; five of 25 recruits failed that criterion. Results concern this selected sample, not untrained learners or an independent replication cohort.

Sequence, primitive-pair and localizer blocks differ in timing and prior exposure. MEG sensor decoding is an observational readout within the task; it does not identify a necessary carrier, anatomical source, tensor binding or a complete nested program.

The paper reports no public raw-data deposit. Selected source-code reading is not a replay: decoder type, smoothing units, position indexing, trial-boundary handling and exclusions require reconciliation. Reported tests and fitted regressions remain publication results.

Prior slower training repeats sequences until correct continuation; the later primitive and localizer blocks use the same participants.
